walkthroughs.body_html:
Unit A2 3: Responding to Music (Set Works and Comparative Study) — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Unit A2 3: Responding to Music (Set Works and Comparative Study) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Unit A2 3: Responding to Music (Set Works and Comparative Study).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A phrase ending with the chord progression V-I forms which cadence?
options: Plagal
Perfect
Imperfect
Interrupted

mcqs.q: An interrupted cadence most typically moves from chord V to which chord?
options: I
VI
IV
II

mcqs.q: What is the strongest evidence to use in a comparative essay on two set works?
options: General adjectives like 'nice' and 'dramatic'
Specific located musical examples from each work
The composers' biographies alone
Your personal taste in music

mcqs.q: A texture made of several independent melodic lines sounding together is called what?
options: Monophonic
Contrapuntal (polyphonic)
Homorhythmic
Unison

mcqs.q: What happens at an interrupted cadence?
options: An interrupted cadence is when the music suddenly stops with a silence.
Chord V resolves unexpectedly, usually to chord VI, deceiving the ear which expected the tonic.
Analysis means copying out the programme note.
An interrupted cadence is when the soloist forgets their entry.

mcqs.q: Is 'the major key makes it happy and the minor key makes it sad' a sufficient analysis?
options: Texture means the material the instruments are made from.
Describing the mood of the music is all an analysis needs.
Analysis means copying out the programme note.
No - credit comes from precise technical observation: keys, cadences, textures, sonorities and structure, with located examples.

mcqs.q: What does 'texture' mean when analysing a set work?
options: Texture means the material the instruments are made from.
The relationship between the simultaneous layers of the music, such as monophonic, homophonic or polyphonic.
Analysis means copying out the programme note.
Texture means how loud or soft the music is.

sequence.def: c.500-1400 — the first period of Western music history
c.1600-1750 — third: opera and the orchestra are born
c.1750-1820 — fourth: symphony and string quartet mature
c.1820-1900 — fifth: programme music and virtuosity
1900 onwards — the most recent period in this list
